function.name: monitor
function.description:
Read output from a background job started via `bash_background`. Returns a snapshot of the job's stdout + stderr lines plus its current status (running / complete with exit code).

### Cursor pattern
First call: omit `since_line` (or pass 0) to read the full buffer.
Follow-up: pass the previous response's `total_lines` as `since_line` to get only what's new — same pattern as `tail -f` against a log.

### Status
- `complete: false` — process is still running. Re-call to get more output.
- `complete: true, exit_code: 0` — finished successfully.
- `complete: true, exit_code: !=0` — finished with an error code; the buffer holds whatever it printed.

since_line.description: Zero-based line index. Omit / pass 0 to read every line; pass the previous call's `total_lines` to read only new lines. Out-of-range values are clamped.
